Every prerequisite ends at a pinned library declaration, an existing supplier/request or a named gap; no stage is claimed closed and no node is implemented.

nodes.title: Finite weighted prime truncation
nodes.statement: Construct S(P,a) : ArithmeticFunction real for a finite set P of natural indices and real weights a. Set S(P,a)(0)=0 and, for n>0, S(P,a)(n)=sum_{p in P} (if p divides n then a(p) else 0). Only the arithmetic interpretation and the prime-power/coprime laws require every member of P to be prime.
hypotheses: P is a finite set; a is real-valued.
proofSteps: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction=ZeroHom carrier. Define the function by the displayed zero guard and finite sum; check its zero field by evaluation.
Export positive evaluation before using the construction in averages. Prove the seven separate API nodes below; do not add an independent arithmetic-function or probability carrier.
acceptance: Zero, positive and empty evaluations agree with the stated convention.
Implement the five tests listed on this node; multiplication in ArithmeticFunction is not used for pointwise products.

nodes.title: Coprime product law
nodes.statement: For prime P and coprime positive m,n, S(P,a)(mn)=S(P,a)(m)+S(P,a)(n).
hypotheses: Every p in P is prime; m,n>0; gcd(m,n)=1.
proofSteps: For p in P, primality gives p divides mn iff p divides m or p divides n.
The two events cannot both hold: a common prime divisor would divide gcd(m,n)=1. Thus their 0/1 indicators add without a double contribution.
Multiply by a(p), sum, and apply positive evaluation at m,n,mn.
acceptance: For P={2}, a(2)=2, m=n=2, the identity fails: the coprimality hypothesis cannot be removed.

nodes.title: Exact divisibility probability
nodes.statement: For every positive d, the real probability mu_N({n : d divides n}) equals (Nat.div N d)/N. This is a probability specialization of existing counting, not a new multiples-counting theorem.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
proofSteps: Apply empiricalMeasure_apply_toReal to the measurable divisibility set on discrete naturals.
Its indicator sum is the real cast of the number of k<N with d dividing k+1. Substitute the already proved Nat.card_multiples and move the finite natural cast through the sum.
acceptance: N=5,d=2 gives 2/5; d>N gives 0; d=1 gives 1.

nodes.title: Signed finite counting error
nodes.statement: Let e_N(d)=mu_N(d divides n)-1/d, in the reals. For d>0, e_N(d)=-(N mod d)/(N*d), so -1/N<e_N(d)<=0; in particular |e_N(d)|<=1/N. This notation is a local expression, not another probability definition.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
proofSteps: Write N=d*(Nat.div N d)+(N mod d) with 0<=N mod d<d.
Substitute the exact probability, cast the quotient-remainder equality to the reals, and divide by positive N*d.
The sign and strict lower bound follow from the remainder bounds. Retain the sign for exact-period specialization.
acceptance: N=5,d=2 gives -1/10. If d divides N the error is exactly zero.

nodes.title: Exact centered pair average
nodes.statement: For positive p,q, let I_d(n) be the real 0/1 indicator of d dividing n. Then integral (I_p-1/p)*(I_q-1/q) dmu_N equals (Nat.div N (Nat.lcm p q))/N -(Nat.div N p)/(N*q) -(Nat.div N q)/(N*p)+1/(p*q).

p,q>0; primality is not needed for this identity.
proofSteps: Convert the integral to its finite average and expand the product into four terms.
The product I_p*I_q is the indicator of the joint divisibility event; the constant term averages to itself because there are exactly N terms.
Use divisibility-probability and joint-divisibility for the three nonconstant terms.
acceptance: When p=q use I_p^2=I_p. When N=5,p=2,q=3 the centered average is -1/15.

nodes.title: Uniform prime-pair error
nodes.statement: For primes p,q, put D(p,q)=1/p-1/p^2 when p=q, and 0 otherwise. Then |integral (I_p-1/p)*(I_q-1/q) dmu_N-D(p,q)|<=2/N. Repeated primes are included.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
p,q prime.
proofSteps: Replace each floor probability in centered-pair-identity by 1/d+e_N(d).
If p=q then lcm(p,p)=p, and the nonerror part is 1/p-1/p^2. If p!=q, coprimality gives lcm(p,q)=p*q and the nonerror part is zero.
The remaining expression is e_N(lcm(p,q))-e_N(p)/q-e_N(q)/p. Each error has magnitude at most 1/N.
Since p,q>=2, 1+1/p+1/q<=2. The triangle inequality proves the bound, including the diagonal.
acceptance: At p=q=2, the centered square equals 1/4 pointwise and the error is actually zero.
Distinct-prime indicators under mu_N need not be independent.

nodes.title: Finite-head second-moment comparison
nodes.statement: For prime P and real a, write A=sum a(p)/p, L=sum |a(p)|, V=sum a(p)^2*(1/p-1/p^2). Then |integral (S(P,a)-A)^2 dmu_N - V| <= 2*L^2/N. This is a centered second moment about A, not a formula for variance about the empirical mean.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
P finite and prime; a real-valued, with no sign or boundedness hypothesis beyond finiteness of P.
proofSteps: For n in the positive sample, S(P,a)(n)-A=sum a(p)*(I_p(n)-1/p).
Square and distribute as a double sum over all ordered pairs (p,q), including the diagonal. Convert the integral to a finite average and interchange these finite sums.
Subtract the sum of a(p)*a(q)*D(p,q). Its off-diagonal terms vanish and its diagonal is exactly V.
Apply centered-pair-error and the triangle inequality, obtaining (2/N)*sum_{p,q}|a(p)|*|a(q)|=(2/N)*L^2. No probabilistic independence or central limit theorem is used.
acceptance: P empty gives 0=0. Signed weights and repeated pair indices must survive expansion.
The bound is useful only when L^2/N is controlled; it is not the Turan-Kubilius inequality and does not discharge the large-prime tail of Erdos-Kac.

nodes.title: Exact moments on complete prime periods
nodes.statement: Under the second-moment-comparison hypotheses, assume Q=product_{p in P}p divides N. Then integral (S(P,a)-A)^2 dmu_N=V. Also the already stated weighted-mean formula gives integral S(P,a) dmu_N=A, so this centered moment is the actual variance in this case.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m, hence a probability on {1,...,N}.
P finite and prime; a real-valued; product_{p in P}p divides N.
proofSteps: Each p in P divides Q and thus N. For p,q in P their lcm divides Q, whether p=q or not.
All three remainder terms in the centered-pair-identity are zero. The exact pair average is D(p,q).
Repeat the explicit finite double-sum argument of second-moment-comparison with equality. The exact first moment follows by replacing each floor quotient by N/p in weighted-mean.
acceptance: For N=6,P={2,3},a(p)=p, A=2 and V=3. For N=5 the corresponding mean is 7/5 and centered second moment is 9/5, so completeness of the period cannot be silently removed.
For P empty, Q=1; every positive N satisfies the condition and both moments vanish.

nodes.title: Simultaneous prime-divisibility probability
nodes.statement: mu_N({n: every p in P divides n}) = floor(N/Q_P)/N.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m. Probabilities below are real-valued.
P is a finite set of natural primes; Q_P is its product, including Q_empty=1.
proofSteps: Distinct members of P are coprime by Nat.coprime_primes. Finset.lcm_eq_prod therefore identifies Q_P with the finite lcm.
By Finset.lcm_dvd_iff, the event of all divisibilities is exactly Q_P dividing n. This also treats P empty: the empty lcm and product are 1.
Every prime is positive, hence Q_P is positive; apply divisibility-probability with d=Q_P. All sets of naturals are measurable.
acceptance: P empty gives probability 1 for every positive N.
P={2,3},N=5 gives 0; N=6 gives 1/6.
Dropping primality fails for P={2,4},N=4: the event has probability 1/4, while floor(4/8)/4=0.

nodes.title: Signed formula for prime-divisibility patterns
nodes.statement: mu_N(E(S,T)) = sum_{U subset T} (-1)^|U| floor(N/Q_{S union U})/N.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m. Probabilities below are real-valued.
S,T are disjoint finite sets of natural primes. Write Q_R=product_{p in R}p, with Q_empty=1; E(S,T)={n: every p in S divides n and no q in T divides n}. These are local expressions, not new carriers.
proofSteps: At each natural n put I_p(n)=1 if p divides n and 0 otherwise. The event indicator is (product_{p in S} I_p(n))*(product_{q in T}(1-I_q(n))).

Apply Finset.prod_one_add with f(q)=-I_q(n), then distribute the first product. The U term is (-1)^|U| times the indicator of all primes in S union U dividing n. Because U is contained in T, it is disjoint from S; repeated indicators would also be idempotent.
Apply empiricalMeasure_apply_toReal to the event and each all-divisibility event; commute the two finite real sums. This avoids any unjustified signed subtraction in extended nonnegative reals.
Use simultaneous-divisibility for S union U, whose members are primes. Natural division is performed before casting to the real normalized probability.
acceptance: T empty recovers simultaneous-divisibility; S=T=empty gives 1.
S={2},T={3},N=5 gives 2/5 rather than the model value 1/3.

nodes.title: Bernoulli-product error for one pattern
nodes.statement: Put b(S,T)=(product_{p in S}1/p)*(product_{q in T}(1-1/q)). Then |mu_N(E(S,T))-b(S,T)| <= 2^|T|/N.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m. Probabilities below are real-valued.
S,T are disjoint finite sets of natural primes. Write Q_R=product_{p in R}p, with Q_empty=1; E(S,T)={n: every p in S divides n and no q in T divides n}. These are local expressions, not new carriers.
proofSteps: For U contained in T, disjointness gives Q_{S union U}=Q_S*Q_U. Positivity permits the reciprocal product identity.
Expand product_{q in T}(1-1/q) with Finset.prod_one_add at f(q)=-1/q. Multiplying by 1/Q_S yields b(S,T)=sum_{U subset T}(-1)^|U|/Q_{S union U}.
Subtract this identity from divisibility-pattern-formula. The difference is sum_{U subset T}(-1)^|U| e_N(Q_{S union U}), with e_N from divisibility-error.
Each product divisor is positive and each error has absolute value at most 1/N. The finite triangle inequality and Finset.card_powerset give 2^|T|/N.
acceptance: No restriction Q_{S union T}<=N is needed for this inequality, but the bound can exceed 1 and then conveys little information.
Disjointness cannot be dropped from the model interpretation: S=T={2} has an empty event while b=1/4, even when N is a multiple of 2.
For N=5,S={2},T={3}, the error is 1/15.

nodes.title: Complete-period Bernoulli law
nodes.statement: If Q_{S union T} divides N, then mu_N(E(S,T))=b(S,T), with b(S,T)=(product_{p in S}1/p)*(product_{q in T}(1-1/q)). Thus the statement for S contained in P and T=P minus S specifies every Boolean divisibility atom for a finite prime set P on a complete period.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m. Probabilities below are real-valued.
S,T are disjoint finite sets of natural primes. Write Q_R=product_{p in R}p, with Q_empty=1; E(S,T)={n: every p in S divides n and no q in T divides n}. These are local expressions, not new carriers.
Q_{S union T} divides N.
proofSteps: For every U contained in T, Q_{S union U} divides Q_{S union T}, hence divides N. Product divisibility follows by splitting the finite product into the subset and its complement.
Each remainder e_N(Q_{S union U}) is zero, by the exact signed remainder in divisibility-error, not just its upper bound.
Use the signed-subset formula and the reciprocal-product expansion from the proof of divisibility-pattern-error. Every summand is now exact, giving b(S,T).

For S contained in P, the sets S and P minus S are disjoint prime sets with union P, so this same equality covers all zero/one coordinate patterns. No new product-measure carrier or theorem about all nonzero residue classes is asserted.
acceptance: N=6,P={2,3}: the atoms none, only 2, only 3, both have probabilities 1/3,1/3,1/6,1/6.
N=5 gives 2/5,2/5,1/5,0; the complete-period hypothesis is essential.
For P empty there is exactly one pattern, of mass 1.

nodes.title: Summed Boolean-atom error
nodes.statement: For a finite prime set P, sum_{S subset P} |mu_N(E(S,P minus S))-b(S,P minus S)| <= 3^|P|/N, with E and b as in divisibility-pattern-error.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; N=m+1; mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k->k+1 at index m. Probabilities below are real-valued.
P is a finite set of natural primes; each S ranges over its powerset, and P minus S is the finite set difference.
proofSteps: For every S contained in P, the disjoint prime sets S and P minus S satisfy divisibility-pattern-error. Their atom error is at most 2^|P minus S|/N.
Sum these inequalities and factor out 1/N. Since S is contained in P, |P minus S|=|P|-|S|.
Apply Finset.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow with real a=1,b=2 to evaluate sum_{S subset P} 2^(|P|-|S|)=3^|P|.

The atoms partition the finite Boolean pattern set and the nonnegative model masses sum to product_{p in P}(1/p+(1-1/p))=1 by finite distributivity. The exported declaration is the displayed sum bound; a measure-theoretic total-variation interface is not introduced.
acceptance: For N=5,P={2,3}, the summed error is 1/3 and the bound is 9/5.
For complete prime periods all atom errors vanish by complete-period-joint-law.
For P empty the summed error is zero. The estimate alone is useful for varying P only when 3^|P|/N is small; it is not a general Kubilius growing-prime theorem.

nodes.title: Exact centered prime-product average
nodes.statement: The mu_N-average of product_{p in P} f_p(n)^alpha_p equals sum_{D subset P} (product_{p in D} w_p)(product_{p in P minus D} v_p) floor(N/Q_D)/N.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes; m is a natural number, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k -> k+1 at index m.

alpha is a natural-valued function on primes, with exponent zero allowed. Put u_p=1/p, f_p(n)=I_p(n)-u_p, v_p=(-u_p)^alpha_p, w_p=(1-u_p)^alpha_p-v_p, and Q_D=product_{p in D} p. All these are local expressions, not new carriers; real arithmetic and empty products equal to one are used.
proofSteps: For each prime p and each n, split on p dividing n to obtain f_p(n)^alpha_p=v_p+w_p I_p(n), also when alpha_p=0.
Apply Finset.prod_add with the w_p I_p(n) term first and v_p second. Products of zero-one indicators give the event that every p in D divides n.

Use integral_empiricalMeasure to replace the integral by the finite average, interchange finite sums, and apply simultaneous-divisibility to D. Every member of D is prime, and the natural quotient N/Q_D is cast to the reals only after division.
The empty subset has Q_D=1 and normalized count one; in particular zero exponents and empty P introduce no exceptional undefined term.
acceptance: All alpha_p=0 gives average one; P empty also gives one.
For P={2},alpha_2=2, v_2=1/4 and w_2=0; the average is exactly 1/4 for every N, including odd N.
For P={2,3},alpha_2=alpha_3=1,N=5 the average is -1/15, not zero.

nodes.title: Explicit centered-product remainder
nodes.statement: Put G(P,alpha)=product_{p in P}(v_p+w_p/p). The absolute difference between the mu_N-average of product f_p^alpha_p and G(P,alpha) is at most [product_{p in P}(|v_p|+|w_p|)-product_{p in P}|v_p|]/N.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes; m is a natural number, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k -> k+1 at index m.

alpha is a natural-valued function on primes, with exponent zero allowed. Put u_p=1/p, f_p(n)=I_p(n)-u_p, v_p=(-u_p)^alpha_p, w_p=(1-u_p)^alpha_p-v_p, and Q_D=product_{p in D} p. All these are local expressions, not new carriers; real arithmetic and empty products equal to one are used.
proofSteps: Expand G by Finset.prod_add with factors w_p/p and v_p; the D coefficient is the same as in centered-product-expansion, multiplied by 1/Q_D. All Q_D are positive.
Subtract the exact centered-product expansion. Each term has coefficient (product_D w_p)(product_{P minus D} v_p) times the signed divisor error e_N(Q_D) from divisibility-error.
For D empty that error is zero because Q_D=1. For every other subset its absolute value is at most 1/N; apply the finite triangle inequality and multiplicativity of absolute value.
Apply Finset.prod_add to |w_p| and |v_p|. The sum of absolute coefficients excluding the empty subset is exactly product(|v_p|+|w_p|)-product|v_p|, which is nonnegative.
acceptance: The bound is zero when P is empty or all alpha_p are zero.
For P={2},alpha_2=2 the bound is zero, recovering the exact square average even when 2 does not divide N.
The model center is G, not a product of empirical centered means; the two-prime N=5 error is 1/15.

nodes.title: Uniform mixed-moment comparison
nodes.statement: With nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, the absolute difference between the mu_N-average of product_{p in P} f_p(n)^alpha_p and product_{p in P}nu_p(alpha_p) is at most (3/2)^|P|/N, for all natural exponents.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes; m is a natural number, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k -> k+1 at index m.

alpha is a natural-valued function on primes, with exponent zero allowed. Put u_p=1/p, f_p(n)=I_p(n)-u_p, v_p=(-u_p)^alpha_p, w_p=(1-u_p)^alpha_p-v_p, and Q_D=product_{p in D} p. All these are local expressions, not new carriers; real arithmetic and empty products equal to one are used.
proofSteps: The identity v_p+w_p/p=nu_p(alpha_p) follows by real ring algebra.
Since p is prime, 0<u_p<=1/2. If alpha_p=0, |v_p|+|w_p|=1. Otherwise pow_le_of_le_one gives u_p^alpha_p<=u_p and (1-u_p)^alpha_p<=1-u_p.
The triangle inequality gives |w_p|<=(1-u_p)^alpha_p+u_p^alpha_p<=1; hence |v_p|+|w_p|<=1+u_p<=3/2. No parity or positive exponent hypothesis is suppressed.
In centered-product-error discard the nonnegative subtracted product, then multiply these nonnegative bounds over P.
acceptance: The estimate permits zero exponents and all N>=1, without a restriction on Q_P.
For alpha_p=1, nu_p(1)=0, but the corresponding arithmetic centered average need not vanish on incomplete periods.
For p=3,e=3, nu_p(e)=2/27; odd individual centered moments are not identically zero.

nodes.title: Complete-period mixed moments
nodes.statement: If Q_P divides N, the mu_N-average of product_{p in P} f_p(n)^alpha_p equals product_{p in P}[u_p(1-u_p)^alpha_p+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^alpha_p] exactly.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes; m is a natural number, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k -> k+1 at index m.

alpha is a natural-valued function on primes, with exponent zero allowed. Put u_p=1/p, f_p(n)=I_p(n)-u_p, v_p=(-u_p)^alpha_p, w_p=(1-u_p)^alpha_p-v_p, and Q_D=product_{p in D} p. All these are local expressions, not new carriers; real arithmetic and empty products equal to one are used.
Q_P divides N.
proofSteps: For every D contained in P, split the prime product into D and its complement to see that Q_D divides Q_P and therefore N.
The signed remainder formula in divisibility-error gives e_N(Q_D)=0. In the exact subset formula every normalized floor can be replaced by 1/Q_D.
Apply Finset.prod_add to factor the resulting sum as product(v_p+w_p/p), then use elementary algebra to obtain the displayed expression.

Each factor is already the centered moment of the existing Bernoulli measure at 1 and 0, by integral_bernoulliMeasure. This interpretation does not introduce a second distribution carrier or claim independence on incomplete periods.
acceptance: N=3,p=3,e=3 gives 2/27, and N=6,P={2,3},both exponents one gives zero.
If any alpha_p=1 the model product vanishes; this is the square-full-support cancellation used in the moment method, not a claim that every square-full product has nonzero model value.
Repeated prime coordinates must be merged into their exponent: p=2 twice gives 1/4, not the product of two zero means.

nodes.title: Finite weighted moment comparison
nodes.statement: Let k>=0 and a:P->R, A=sum_{p in P}a(p)/p, and L=sum_{p in P}|a(p)|. For each ordered tuple t:{0,...,k-1}->P let T_t be its image, alpha_t(p) the number of coordinates equal to p, and G(t)=product_{p in T_t}nu_p(alpha_t(p)), with nu_p(e)=(1/p)(1-1/p)^e+(1-1/p)(-1/p)^e. Put M_k=sum_t (product_{j<k}a(t(j)))G(t). Then |integral (S(P,a)(n)-A)^k dmu_N - M_k| <= (3/2)^k L^k/N. S(P,a) is the existing zero-extended primeDivisibilitySum; all auxiliary expressions are local finite sums/products.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, a has arbitrary real weights (including negative and zero values), m,k are natural numbers, N=m+1, and mu_N samples 1,...,N.
Tuples are ordered and can repeat primes. The empty tuple exists when k=0 even if P is empty, so M_0=1 and L^0=1. When P is empty and k>0 the tuple set is empty and M_k=0.
proofSteps: At every sampled n>0, positive-evaluation gives S(P,a)(n)-A=sum_{p in P}a(p)f_p(n). Apply Finset.sum_pow' and integral_empiricalMeasure, commuting finite sums.

For a tuple t, apply Finset.prod_fiberwise_of_maps_to' with target its image to group product_j f_{t(j)}(n) into product_{p in T_t}f_p(n)^alpha_t(p). Distinct image primes satisfy centered-product-uniform-error.
Finset.card_image_le gives |T_t|<=k. Since 3/2>=1, pow_le_pow_right₀ bounds (3/2)^|T_t| by (3/2)^k. Multiply by |product_j a(t(j))| and sum using the triangle inequality.
Finset.sum_pow' applied to |a| evaluates sum_t product_j |a(t(j))|=L^k, yielding the claimed bound, also in the empty-index cases.

The model interpretation uses existing integral_bernoulliMeasure and iIndepFun.integral_fun_prod_comp: for an independent Bernoulli(1/p) family, first group each repeated coordinate into its power, then factor only across distinct primes. Thus M_k is its weighted centered k-th moment. This interpretation is already generic library mathematics; it is not a separate node or an independence assumption on mu_N.
acceptance: For k=0 both arithmetic and model moments equal one; for P empty and k>0 both vanish.
For P={3},a(3)=-1,k=3,N=3, both sides' moments are -2/27. Taking absolute weights inside the model would be wrong.
For k=2 the model is sum a(p)^2(1/p-1/p^2). Keep the inherited sharper error 2L^2/N; the new general bound gives 9L^2/(4N), not an improvement in that special case.
A Gaussian approximation needs separate pairing/collision estimates and normalization; this finite comparison is not an Erdos-Kac theorem.

sources.match: Follows the source's ordered tuple expansion and multiplicity grouping, specialized to the positive integer sample. The explicit finite error (3/2)^k L^k/N is derived here; no Gaussian asymptotic or general sieve-multiset theorem is imported.

nodes.title: Centered prime factor bounds
nodes.statement: For a natural prime p and e>=2, 0<=nu_p(e)<=v_p.
hypotheses: Write u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e and v_p=u_p(1-u_p). These are local expressions, not new carriers. Since p is prime, 0<u_p<=1/2.
The exponent is a natural number at least two. No assertion of vanishing for odd exponents is made.
proofSteps: Write e=j+2 and factor nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)((1-u_p)^(j+1)-(-u_p)^(j+1)).
Since 0<=u_p<=1-u_p<=1, power monotonicity and the absolute-value bound give a nonnegative bracket. Each of the two absolute powers is bounded by its base, so the bracket is at most (1-u_p)+u_p=1.
Multiply by v_p>=0. Direct algebra also gives nu_p(0)=1, nu_p(1)=0 and nu_p(2)=v_p; these evaluations are routine uses of the expression, not new definitions.
acceptance: At p=3,e=3 and e=4 the factor is 2/27, positive and at most 2/9.
At p=2 all odd factors vanish, while e=2 gives 1/4.
Do not extend the conclusion to signed weighted factors a(p)^e.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: The source bounds local centered factors for exponents at least two. The sharper bound by v_p, including odd nonnegativity for u_p<=1/2, is derived here.

nodes.title: Prime model multinomial expansion
nodes.statement: Let M_k be the inherited unit-weight ordered-tuple model: sum over t:{0,...,k-1}->P of product_{p in image(t)}nu_p(|t^{-1}(p)|). Then M_k=sum_{alpha in piAntidiag(P,k)} multinomial(P,alpha) product_{p in P}nu_p(alpha(p)). Here piAntidiag consists of natural-valued functions, zero off P, with total k; multinomial(P,alpha)=k!/product_{p in P}alpha(p)!.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
k is any natural number, including zero. The empty tuple and zero multiplicity assignment both contribute one when k=0.
proofSteps: Use the positive complete period N=product_{p in P}p (equal to one for empty P). The existing complete-period-centered-product formula evaluates every mixed product exactly.

Expand the centered prime sum to the k-th power once with Finset.sum_pow' and group repeated positions by image fibers, as in weighted-moment-comparison. Integrating gives M_k exactly, because this chosen period is complete.
Expand the same power with Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag and integrate term by term. Complete-period-centered-product gives the stated multinomial sum. Equate these two finite averages.

This argument imports the generic multinomial identity and uses an auxiliary complete period only to identify finite model expressions. It makes no independence assertion at an arbitrary empirical sample length.
acceptance: M_0=1 also for empty P; M_k=0 for empty P and k>0.
For P={2,3}, k=4, the expression is 203/432, not its paired contribution 1/3.
An assignment with some multiplicity one contributes zero; zero multiplicities contribute factors one.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: Repackages the source's ordered-tuple/fiber expansion through Mathlib's existing multinomial theorem; not a new general combinatorial theorem.

nodes.title: Paired prime contribution
nodes.statement: For r>=0 let H_r=sum_{S subset P, |S|=r} product_{p in S}v_p. The portion of the multinomial model M_(2r) over assignments alpha(p) in {0,2} is ((2r)!/2^r) H_r.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
The portion means the sum of multinomial(P,alpha) product_{p in P}nu_p(alpha(p)) over alpha in piAntidiag(P,2r) satisfying the displayed multiplicity restriction.
proofSteps: Such an assignment is uniquely determined by S={p in P:alpha(p)=2}; its total forces |S|=r, and conversely each r-subset gives an assignment.
At that assignment nu_p(0)=1 and nu_p(2)=v_p. The product of multiplicity factorials is 2^r.
Use Nat.multinomial_spec to identify the coefficient with (2r)!/2^r in the reals. Reindex the finite sum by the r-subsets. For r=0 all products and factorials are one.
acceptance: For P={2,3},r=2 the contribution is 6(1/4)(2/9)=1/3.
For |P|<r it is zero; this is not the whole even moment.
The r=0 formula remains one for empty P.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: Exact finite paired-support specialization of the source's even-moment leading term; lower-support terms are deliberately retained separately.

nodes.title: Distinct prime variance tuples
nodes.statement: For r>=0 put D_r=sum over injective t:{0,...,r-1}->P of product_{j<r}v_{t(j)}. Then D_r=r! H_r, where H_r sums products of v_p over r-element subsets of P.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
The tuple is ordered and injective. Empty-index sums/products use the usual conventions.
proofSteps: Group the injective tuples by image S. Only r-subsets occur.
For each S the fiber consists of bijections from Fin r to the subtype of elements of S. Since |S|=r, fix one such equivalence and apply Fintype.card_equiv to get exactly r! bijections.
The product along every such bijection is product_{p in S}v_p. Sum the constant fiber values, also handling the unique empty bijection at r=0.
acceptance: For P={3},r=2 the tuple set is empty.
For P={2,3},r=2 the two orders contribute 1/9 in total.
For r=0 both D_r and H_r are one.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: The source switches between distinct ordered primes and unordered supports. This arithmetic-weight specialization uses existing equivalence cardinalities; it does not plan a new generic permutation count.

nodes.title: Prime variance collision estimate
nodes.statement: For r>=2, with D_r the injective ordered variance tuple sum, 0<=V^r-D_r<=binom(r,2) Q V^(r-2).
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
No lower bound on V and no nonemptiness hypothesis on P are needed; there is no division by V.
proofSteps: Expand V^r as the sum of products over all ordered r-tuples. Nonnegative weights show the injective sub-sum is at most the full sum.
A noninjective tuple has some equal pair of distinct positions. Bound its weight by the sum of its memberships in those collision events; this is a finite union bound with multiplicities allowed.
For a fixed two-position subset, sum first over the common prime. Its squared weight sums to Q. The remaining r-2 freely chosen positions contribute V^(r-2).
Finset.card_powersetCard counts the two-position subsets as binom(r,2). Add their equal contributions. The r=2 empty remaining product is one even if V=0.
acceptance: For r=2 the difference is exactly Q.
For P={3},r=2 the difference is (2/9)^2.
Empty P satisfies the inequality, including r=2 with exponent zero.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: A finite variance-weighted refinement of the source's distinct-prime product estimate. The explicit Q collision term is derived here, not quoted as the source's displayed bound.

nodes.title: Fixed prime support moment bound
nodes.statement: Let S be a nonempty finite prime set of size s and k>=2s. Sum over alpha in piAntidiag(S,k) with alpha(p)>=2 on S, writing B=sum_alpha multinomial(S,alpha) product_{p in S}nu_p(alpha(p)). Then 0<=B<=k! binom(k-s-1,s-1) (product_{p in S}v_p)/2^s.
hypotheses: S is a finite set of natural primes. Write u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e and v_p=u_p(1-u_p). These are local expressions.
s=|S|>=1 and k>=2s are essential for the exact composition count. Values of alpha off S are zero.
proofSteps: Set beta(p)=alpha(p)-2 on S and zero off S. This gives a bijection with the nonnegative assignments of total k-2s on S.

Read the existing piAntidiag/finsuppAntidiag correspondence and apply card_finsuppAntidiag_nat_eq_choose. The count is binom(s+(k-2s)-1,k-2s)=binom(k-s-1,s-1), not the larger printed count in the author copy.

Every local factor lies in [0,v_p] by local-factor-bound. Every alpha(p)! is at least 2, so their product is at least 2^s. Nat.multinomial_spec therefore bounds the nonnegative real coefficient by k!/2^s.
Bound each summand by k! product v_p/2^s and multiply by the exact number of assignments. All denominators are positive.
acceptance: For s=2,k=5 the admissible multiplicities are (2,3) and (3,2), so the count is two, not three.
For k=2s the only assignment is constantly two.
For S={3},k=4 the actual contribution is 2/27; the bound is an upper bound, not an identity.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: Decomposes the source's lower-support estimate while applying the already-recorded source finding E2. Replacing the source's local bound by v_p gives the stated finite refinement.

nodes.title: Smaller prime support bound
nodes.statement: For k>=1 let B_k be the part of the multinomial model over assignments with support size at most floor((k-1)/2). Define R_k=k! sum_{s=1}^{floor((k-1)/2)} binom(k-s-1,s-1) V^s/(2^s s!). Then 0<=B_k<=R_k.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
The support of an assignment is {p in P:alpha(p) is nonzero}; all sums use natural multiplicities of total k. For k=1 or 2 the displayed s-sum is empty and R_k=0.
proofSteps: Since k>0, every assignment has nonempty support. If any multiplicity equals one, its factor nu_p(1) is zero, so discard such terms.

Group the remaining assignments by their support S. Outside S the zero-multiplicity factors and factorials are one. Apply fixed-support-bound with s=|S|, since all nonzero multiplicities are at least two.
Sum over all s-subsets to obtain k! binom(k-s-1,s-1) H_s/2^s for each permitted s.
From distinct-prime-tuples and nonnegative weights, s! H_s=D_s<=V^s by inclusion among all tuples and Finset.sum_pow'. Divide by positive s! and sum over s to obtain R_k.
acceptance: For k=1,2 there are no nonzero smaller-support terms.
For P={2,3},k=4 the smaller-support contribution is 1/16+2/27=59/432.
For odd k there is no all-paired support; every nonzero model summand belongs to this bound.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: Finite version of the source's smaller-support summation preceding estimate (11), using the corrected exact count and variance weights. It does not claim the source's uniform asymptotic range.

nodes.title: Finite even Gaussian moment bound
nodes.statement: For r>=2, N=m+1 and A=sum_{p in P}1/p, let C_(2r)=(2r)!/(2^r r!), epsilon_k=(3/2)^k |P|^k/N, and R_k=k! sum_{s=1}^{floor((k-1)/2)} binom(k-s-1,s-1) V^s/(2^s s!). Then |integral (S(P,1)-A)^(2r) dmu_N - centralMoment(id,2r,gaussianReal(0,V))| <= epsilon_(2r)+C_(2r) binom(r,2) Q V^(r-2)+R_(2r). The Gaussian variance argument is the nonnegative real V, not its square root.
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
m is natural and mu_N samples exactly 1,...,N. S is the existing zero-extended primeDivisibilitySum with unit weights. r>=2, so the zero-th and sharper second-moment results remain inherited.
Use the existing Gaussian measure and centralMoment carrier; V>=0 identifies Real.toNNReal V with V, including the degenerate empty-prime case.
proofSteps: The inherited weighted-moment-comparison at unit weights bounds the arithmetic moment minus M_(2r) by epsilon_(2r).
Use model-multinomial-expansion. A singleton exponent kills its term. All other supports have size at most r; a support of size exactly r must have every exponent two.
Use paired-support-formula and distinct-prime-tuples to write that leading part as C_(2r) D_r; smaller-support-bound bounds the nonnegative remainder by R_(2r).
Prime-collision-bound controls |C_(2r)D_r-C_(2r)V^r| by the collision term. The coefficient is nonnegative.

Tau Ceti's existing even Gaussian central-moment theorem evaluates the target as V^r (2r-1)!!. The pinned factorial/double-factorial identities identify this with C_(2r)V^r. Add the three errors by the triangle inequality.
acceptance: For P={2,3}, V=17/36, model fourth moment=203/432 and Gaussian fourth moment=289/432; their difference is -43/216.
Empty P has zero positive-order moments and zero right-hand side.
This is a finite unweighted estimate. It does not establish Mertens normalization, large-prime removal, a growing-order asymptotic range or convergence in distribution.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: Builds the arithmetic finite-error comparison into the source's paired/smaller-support method. Explicit epsilon and Q terms are derived; the generic Gaussian evaluation is imported.

nodes.title: Finite odd prime moment bound
nodes.statement: For r>=0, N=m+1, A=sum_{p in P}1/p and k=2r+1, |integral (S(P,1)-A)^k dmu_N| <= (3/2)^k |P|^k/N + R_k, where R_k=k! sum_{s=1}^{floor((k-1)/2)} binom(k-s-1,s-1) V^s/(2^s s!).
hypotheses: P is a finite set of natural primes, u_p=1/p, nu_p(e)=u_p(1-u_p)^e+(1-u_p)(-u_p)^e, v_p=u_p(1-u_p), V=sum_{p in P}v_p and Q=sum_{p in P}v_p^2. These are local expressions, not new carriers. In particular 0<u_p<=1/2 and v_p>=0.
mu_N samples exactly the positive integers 1,...,N; S is the existing unit-weight finite prime sum. The absolute value is required even though the unit-weight model odd moment is nonnegative.
proofSteps: Use model-multinomial-expansion and nu_p(1)=0. A nonzero summand has all nonzero multiplicities at least two, so its support size is at most floor(k/2)=r.
Because k is odd, there is no all-paired support of size k/2. Thus the entire M_k equals B_k from smaller-support-bound, giving 0<=M_k<=R_k.
Apply the inherited unit-weight moment comparison and the triangle inequality. This uses the nonnegative model, not a nonnegativity assertion about the arithmetic moment.
The existing odd Gaussian central-moment theorem evaluates the comparison target as zero. It is a supplier interpretation, not a new Gaussian theorem.
acceptance: For P={3},N=3,k=3 the arithmetic/model moment is 2/27, not zero.
For P={3},N=1,k=3 the arithmetic moment is -1/27.
For r=0, R_1=0; the inherited first-mean estimate is sharper than the displayed 3/2 bound.
For empty P every positive-order moment and bound vanish.

sources.locator: Author copy, proof of Proposition 2, internal pp.4-6; pairing and smaller-support discussion on p.5
sources.match: Finite parity specialization of the source's lower-support argument. No symmetry of the arithmetic divisibility variables is assumed.

nodes.title: Prime cutoff decomposition of omega
nodes.statement: For every n>0 and z>=0, omega(n)=S(P_z,1)(n)+|T_z(n)|. In particular a prime equal to z is retained, and every prime power contributes once, not its exponent.
hypotheses: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors as omega and existing unit-weight primeDivisibilitySum S. No new prime-count, cutoff, moment or measure carrier is introduced.

For real z>=0, P_z denotes the existing Nat.primesLE(floor_nat(z)); a prime p belongs precisely when p<=z. On positive n put T_z(n)={p in n.primeFactors: z<p}, A_z=sum_{p in P_z}1/p, and Y_z(n)=S(P_z,1)(n)-A_z. All casts, logarithms and error terms are real.
n is a positive natural number. The identity needs only z>=0, not z>1.
proofSteps: Use positive-evaluation to express S(P_z,1)(n) as a sum of divisibility indicators. Nat.mem_primesLE and Nat.le_floor_iff identify its nonzero terms with the members of n.primeFactors whose real value is at most z, using Nat.mem_primeFactors and n>0.
Use omega-compatibility and positive-evaluation on n.primeFactors to express omega(n) as the cardinality of that finite set.
Partition n.primeFactors by p<=z and z<p; add their cardinalities. This uses finite-set partition identities, not an asymptotic estimate.
acceptance: At n=60,z=3 the head is 2 and the tail is 1; at z=5 the tail is 0.
At n=8,z=3/2 the head is 0 and tail is 1, not 3; n=1 gives two zero summands.

sources.locator: Author copy, internal p.4, Deduction of Theorem 1, first three displayed formulas and Cauchy–Schwarz step
sources.match: Exact auxiliary decomposition of the source's displayed split into p<=z and p>z. Real cutoffs are represented by the existing natural floor and primesLE. The source's O(k) is not assumed.

nodes.title: Logarithmic bound for discarded prime factors
nodes.statement: For n>0 and z>1, |T_z(n)| <= log(n)/log(z). The bound counts distinct prime divisors; it permits n=1 and real nonintegral z, and has no assumption z<=n.
hypotheses: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors as omega and existing unit-weight primeDivisibilitySum S. No new prime-count, cutoff, moment or measure carrier is introduced.

For real z>=0, P_z denotes the existing Nat.primesLE(floor_nat(z)); a prime p belongs precisely when p<=z. On positive n put T_z(n)={p in n.primeFactors: z<p}, A_z=sum_{p in P_z}1/p, and Y_z(n)=S(P_z,1)(n)-A_z. All casts, logarithms and error terms are real.
n is positive and z>1, so log(z)>0.
proofSteps: For T=T_z(n), Nat.mem_primeFactors supplies prime, positive divisors of n. The existing Finset.prod_primes_dvd proves product T divides n. Its positive product is at most n.
Every p in T satisfies log(z)<=log(p) by Real.log_le_log, so |T| log(z)<=sum_{p in T}log(p).

Apply Real.log_prod to identify the sum with log(product T), then Real.log_le_log to bound this by log(n). Divide by the positive Real.log_pos z. The empty product is one, so no nonempty-tail hypothesis is used.
acceptance: At n=1 the estimate is 0<=0; z>n gives empty T.
At n=30,z=2 the tail count is 2, consistent with 2 log(2)<=log(30).
The logarithmic quotient is not claimed for z=1 or for n=0.

sources.locator: Author copy, internal p.4, Deduction of Theorem 1, first three displayed formulas and Cauchy–Schwarz step
sources.match: Explicit deterministic bound underlying the source's O(k) tail when z=x^(1/k). This is a derived auxiliary with exact hypotheses, not a quoted numbered inequality.

nodes.title: Centered prime cutoff error
nodes.statement: For N=m+1, z>1, b real, and 1<=n<=N, set D=log(N)/log(z)+|A_z-b|. Then |(omega(n)-b)-Y_z(n)|<=D. The two summands in D respectively control discarded primes and the change of center.
hypotheses: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors as omega and existing unit-weight primeDivisibilitySum S. No new prime-count, cutoff, moment or measure carrier is introduced.

For real z>=0, P_z denotes the existing Nat.primesLE(floor_nat(z)); a prime p belongs precisely when p<=z. On positive n put T_z(n)={p in n.primeFactors: z<p}, A_z=sum_{p in P_z}1/p, and Y_z(n)=S(P_z,1)(n)-A_z. All casts, logarithms and error terms are real.
m is natural, N=m+1; b is any real center, not an assumed empirical or model mean. z>1 and 1<=n<=N.
proofSteps: Omega-cutoff-identity gives (omega(n)-b)-Y_z(n)=|T_z(n)|+(A_z-b). Apply the triangle inequality and nonnegativity of a finite cardinality.
Use large-prime-log-bound and Real.log_le_log for n<=N, dividing by log(z)>0. This proves the displayed D bound.
D is nonnegative because N>=1. No Mertens estimate for |A_z-b|, and no numerical choice of b or z, is inserted without a separate proof.
acceptance: For b=A_z, the pointwise difference is exactly the nonnegative tail count.
For n=N=1, the log contribution vanishes; the error equals |A_z-b|, even when P_z contains primes absent from the sample.
A center mismatch is retained even if every prime factor lies below the cutoff.

sources.locator: Author copy, internal p.4, Deduction of Theorem 1, first three displayed formulas and Cauchy–Schwarz step
sources.match: Quantifies both terms inside the source's O(k), without borrowing the unstated Mertens normalization. It is valid beyond the source's special cutoff.

nodes.title: Binomial prime cutoff power error
nodes.statement: For N=m+1, z>1, b real, 1<=n<=N and k>=0, with D as above, |(omega(n)-b)^k-Y_z(n)^k| <= sum_{j=0}^{k-1} binom(k,j) D^(k-j) |Y_z(n)|^j. The sum is empty at k=0.
hypotheses: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors as omega and existing unit-weight primeDivisibilitySum S. No new prime-count, cutoff, moment or measure carrier is introduced.

For real z>=0, P_z denotes the existing Nat.primesLE(floor_nat(z)); a prime p belongs precisely when p<=z. On positive n put T_z(n)={p in n.primeFactors: z<p}, A_z=sum_{p in P_z}1/p, and Y_z(n)=S(P_z,1)(n)-A_z. All casts, logarithms and error terms are real.
m,k are natural, z>1, b real and 1<=n<=m+1. D=log(m+1)/log(z)+|A_z-b|.
proofSteps: Let d=(omega(n)-b)-Y_z(n). The preceding centered-cutoff-error gives |d|<=D and D>=0.
Apply the pinned binomial theorem to (Y_z(n)+d)^k. Isolate its j=k term, which is Y_z(n)^k, leaving exactly j<k; at k=0 both the remainder and its bound are zero.

Apply Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs. Replace the absolute value of each product by binom(k,j)|Y_z(n)|^j|d|^(k-j), and use monotonicity of nonnegative powers to replace |d| by D. Signs of Y and d are not discarded before this step.
acceptance: For k=0 the bound is 0; for k=1 it is D, and for k=2 it is D^2+2D|Y|.
When Y is negative, |Y| cannot be replaced by Y in the bound. At n=1,N=2,z=3,b=A_z,k=2, Y=-5/6 and 0<D=log(2)/log(3)<1, so D^2+2DY is negative.

sources.locator: Author copy, internal p.4, Deduction of Theorem 1, first three displayed formulas and Cauchy–Schwarz step
sources.match: Exact finite binomial-error version of the source's second displayed formula. No unspecified O-constant, asymptotic order range or moment convergence is assumed.

nodes.title: Odd absolute prime moments from adjacent even moments
nodes.statement: For m,r natural, finite P, real weights a and real b, let Z(n)=S(P,a)(n)-b and E_j=integral Z^j dmu_(m+1). Then integral |Z|^(2r+1) dmu_(m+1) <= sqrt(E_(2r)*E_(2r+2)). Both even factors are nonnegative. At r=0, E_0=1.
hypotheses: mu_(m+1) is the existing empirical probability measure on 1,...,m+1.
P is any finite set of natural indices, a has arbitrary real values and b is real. No primality or independence hypothesis is needed for this finite-sample inequality.
proofSteps: Rewrite all three integrals using the existing integral_empiricalMeasure. Every real function on the discrete natural carrier is strongly measurable; each resulting sum is finite.
Apply the existing Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq to f(n)=|Z(n)|^r and g(n)=|Z(n)|^(r+1) over the N=m+1 sample indices. Their product is |Z|^(2r+1), and their squares equal Z^(2r) and Z^(2r+2).

Divide the squared Cauchy–Schwarz inequality by N^2. The same positive normalization occurs in each average. Nonnegative square roots and Real.sq_sqrt give the stated bound. This is an arithmetic specialization, not a new generic Cauchy–Schwarz theorem.
acceptance: For P={2},a=1,b=1/2 all |Z| equal 1/2, so equality holds for every N and r.
For P={3},N=3,a=1,b=1/3, the signed first moment is 0 but the absolute first moment is 4/9; the r=0 upper bound is sqrt(2/9).
Signed weights and constant nonzero centers are allowed. An empty P with b=0 gives zero odd absolute moments, while E_0 remains 1.

sources.locator: Author copy, internal p.4, Deduction of Theorem 1, first three displayed formulas and Cauchy–Schwarz step
sources.match: Specializes the source's Cauchy–Schwarz step, retaining the absolute moment rather than incorrectly using its possibly vanishing signed odd moment. Existing finite Cauchy–Schwarz supplies the generic theorem.

nodes.title: Finite prime cutoff moment transfer
nodes.statement: For N=m+1, z>1, b real and k>=0, put D=log(N)/log(z)+|A_z-b|, E_j=integral Y_z^j dmu_N, and U_j=E_j for even j, while U_j=sqrt(E_(j-1)*E_(j+1)) for odd j. Then |integral (omega-b)^k dmu_N-E_k| <= sum_{j=0}^{k-1} binom(k,j) D^(k-j) U_j. The formula is an exact finite bound with no unspecified constant.
hypotheses: Use the existing ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors as omega and existing unit-weight primeDivisibilitySum S. No new prime-count, cutoff, moment or measure carrier is introduced.

For real z>=0, P_z denotes the existing Nat.primesLE(floor_nat(z)); a prime p belongs precisely when p<=z. On positive n put T_z(n)={p in n.primeFactors: z<p}, A_z=sum_{p in P_z}1/p, and Y_z(n)=S(P_z,1)(n)-A_z. All casts, logarithms and error terms are real.
m,k are natural, N=m+1, z>1 and b is real. E_j and U_j are local expressions, not new moment carriers. For odd j, j>=1 and j-1,j+1 are even.
proofSteps: Rewrite the integral difference as the difference of the two empirical finite averages. Apply the triangle inequality for that finite sum and cutoff-power-error at every n=1,...,N.
Interchange the two finite sums and pull out the nonnegative constant binom(k,j)D^(k-j). The remaining factor is the empirical absolute j-th moment of Y_z.
For even j, |Y_z|^j=Y_z^j. For odd j=2r+1, apply absolute-odd-moment at P=P_z, weights 1 and center A_z. This proves the U_j bound without any iid premise.

At k=0 both original moments are 1 and the right side is empty. For later asymptotics, even U_j inputs can use second-moment-comparison and finite-even-gaussian-bound; their growth and D's size must still be established, and are not conclusions of this theorem.
acceptance: At k=0 the two normalized moments equal 1; at k=1 the right side is D because U_0=1.
At k=2 the bound is D^2+2D sqrt(E_2), since E_0=1.
The formula holds for N=1 and for z>N; it does not remove the separate center discrepancy |A_z-b|.
No convergence in distribution, Mertens estimate or uniform growing-order range follows without additional bounds.

nodes.title: Exact residue probability
nodes.statement: For every a in ZMod d, p(a)=[floor(N/d)+1_{rho(a)<R}]/N. Natural division is taken before the real cast. The shift rho(a)=(a-1).val is essential because the sample starts at 1.
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

d is a positive natural modulus; a ranges over the existing ZMod d. Put R=N mod d and rho(a)=(a-1).val, so 0<=rho(a)<d. Put p(a)=mu_N({n : the cast of n in ZMod d equals a}). These are local expressions, not new definitions.
proofSteps: For each sample index k<N, cast(k+1)=a is equivalent to cast(k)=a-1, hence to k congruent to rho(a) modulo d, by natCast_zmod_val and natCast_eq_natCast_iff.
Apply the existing empiricalMeasure_apply_toReal. Its finite indicator sum is the natural count of this congruence predicate, cast to the reals.
Use the existing Nat.count_modEq_card with b=N and v=rho(a); val_lt reduces rho(a) mod d to rho(a). No interval-counting or CRT theorem is being replanned.
acceptance: N=5,d=3: masses at residues 0,1,2 are 1/5,2/5,2/5.
d=1 gives mass 1. For N<d the supported residues are 1,...,N, not 0,...,N-1.

nodes.title: Residue atom error
nodes.statement: For every a, |p(a)-1/d|<1/N. More precisely the proof computes the signed difference as [1_{rho(a)<R}-R/d]/N; its sign depends on the residue.
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

d is a positive natural modulus; a ranges over the existing ZMod d. Put R=N mod d and rho(a)=(a-1).val, so 0<=rho(a)<d. Put p(a)=mu_N({n : the cast of n in ZMod d equals a}). These are local expressions, not new definitions.
proofSteps: Cast N=d*floor(N/d)+R to the reals and substitute residue-probability.
If rho(a)<R, then R>0 and the error is (d-R)/(N*d), strictly between 0 and 1/N. Otherwise the error is -R/(N*d), between -1/N and 0, since 0<=R<d. At R=0 both are zero.
acceptance: At N=5,d=3, residue 1 has positive error 1/15 while residue 0 has negative error -2/15.
For residue zero this specializes to the inherited signed divisibility error; it does not extend its nonpositive sign to all residues.

nodes.title: Exact summed residue error
nodes.statement: The finite sum over all a in ZMod d of |p(a)-1/d| equals 2*R*(d-R)/(N*d). Thus it vanishes on complete periods. If N<d it is exactly 2*(1-N/d).
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

d is a positive natural modulus; a ranges over the existing ZMod d. Put R=N mod d and rho(a)=(a-1).val, so 0<=rho(a)<d. Put p(a)=mu_N({n : the cast of n in ZMod d equals a}). These are local expressions, not new definitions.
proofSteps: The translation a mapped to a-1 is a permutation. Composing with the native equivalence between ZMod d and Fin d shows exactly R residues satisfy rho(a)<R, and d-R do not.
The signed differences computed in residue-atom-error have absolute values (d-R)/(N*d) on the first group and R/(N*d) on the second. Sum the two constants with their group cardinalities and simplify.

At R=0 the sum is zero. If N<d, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt gives R=N and cancellation gives the displayed specialization. The exported Lean equality is the general exact formula; these specializations are acceptance consequences.
acceptance: N=5,d=3 gives 4/15. N=2,d=5 gives 6/5; summed absolute error can exceed 1.
N=6,d=3 and d=1 give zero. Half this finite sum is the finite-law total variation; no new variation carrier is defined.

nodes.title: Sharp residue event bound
nodes.statement: For every subset A of ZMod d, |mu_N({n : cast(n) belongs to A})-|A|/d| <= R*(d-R)/(N*d). The bound is attained by A={a : rho(a)<R}.
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

d is a positive natural modulus; a ranges over the existing ZMod d. Put R=N mod d and rho(a)=(a-1).val, so 0<=rho(a)<d. Put p(a)=mu_N({n : the cast of n in ZMod d equals a}). These are local expressions, not new definitions.
A is represented by a Finset of the finite native residue carrier.
proofSteps: Partition the empirical event into its disjoint residue atoms and sum their probabilities, using finite empirical indicators.
The sum of all signed differences is zero. Each positive atom error is (d-R)/(N*d) and there are R such atoms; their total is R*(d-R)/(N*d). The negative total is its negative.
The sum over any A lies between these negative and positive totals. The heavy-residue set selects exactly the positive errors, giving equality, including R=0 with an empty set.
acceptance: N=5,d=3,A={1,2}: discrepancy is 2/15, exactly half the summed error.
Empty and full A have zero error; cardinality is taken in ZMod d, so duplicate integer representatives do not count twice.

nodes.title: Bounded residue statistic bound
nodes.statement: For F:ZMod d->R and real L<=U with L<=F(a)<=U for every a, |integral F(cast(n)) dmu_N - (1/d) sum_a F(a)| <= (U-L)*R*(d-R)/(N*d).
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

d is a positive natural modulus; a ranges over the existing ZMod d. Put R=N mod d and rho(a)=(a-1).val, so 0<=rho(a)<d. Put p(a)=mu_N({n : the cast of n in ZMod d equals a}). These are local expressions, not new definitions.
L,U are real with L<=U and F has pointwise values in [L,U].
proofSteps: Use integral_empiricalMeasure and regroup the finite sample by its residue, obtaining sum_a F(a)*p(a). Subtract the uniform finite mean.
The atom errors sum to zero, so replacing F by F-L leaves the discrepancy unchanged. This shifted function lies between 0 and U-L.

Split the finite sum by the sign of the atom errors. Its positive and negative bounds are (U-L) times the common positive error mass computed in residue-event-error. Apply the absolute-value bound. All integrals are finite empirical integrals; no target measurability or integrability assumption is missing.
acceptance: Constant F has exactly zero error even if its constant is negative.
At N=5,d=3 take F=1 on {1,2} and -1 on {0}: the error is 4/15, attained with U-L=2.

nodes.title: Joint residue atom formula
nodes.statement: For every residue tuple a, put c=E^{-1}(a) in ZMod Q. Then J(a)=[floor(N/Q)+1_{(c-1).val<R}]/N.
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

I is any finite index type, possibly empty; q:I->N has positive values and is pairwise coprime. Put Q=product_i q(i), R=N mod Q, E=ZMod.prodEquivPi q, and J(a)=mu_N({n : for every i, the cast of n in ZMod(q(i)) equals a(i)}). The tuple a lies in the native dependent product of ZMod(q(i)). Moduli 1 and composite coprime moduli are allowed.
proofSteps: The native ring equivalence E takes cast(n) to the tuple of its coordinate casts, by prodEquivPi_apply and preservation of natural casts. Injectivity identifies the entire tuple event with the single event cast(n)=E^{-1}(a).
Every q(i)>0 implies Q>0, including the empty product Q=1. Apply residue-probability at Q. This is a probability specialization of an implemented CRT, not a new CRT construction.
acceptance: For q=(2,3),N=5, tuple (0,0) has mass 0 and tuple (1,1) mass 1/5.
The empty index type has one tuple of probability 1. Noncoprime q=(2,4) is excluded: incompatible tuples cannot have uniform positive mass.

nodes.title: Complete-period joint residue law
nodes.statement: If Q divides N, every tuple a has J(a)=product_i(1/q(i)). These atom identities are exactly the joint uniform product law on the finite residue spaces.
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

I is any finite index type, possibly empty; q:I->N has positive values and is pairwise coprime. Put Q=product_i q(i), R=N mod Q, E=ZMod.prodEquivPi q, and J(a)=mu_N({n : for every i, the cast of n in ZMod(q(i)) equals a(i)}). The tuple a lies in the native dependent product of ZMod(q(i)). Moduli 1 and composite coprime moduli are allowed.
Q divides N.
proofSteps: The divisibility assumption makes R zero, so crt-residue-probability gives J(a)=1/Q.

Move the natural product through the real cast and invert it to obtain product_i(1/q(i)). Every factor is nonzero. Finite tuples exhaust all outcomes, so these atom masses specify the joint product law.

Summing over any coordinate rectangle factors into the product of coordinate uniform probabilities by the existing finite product-of-sums identity. In particular, the all-zero tuple on distinct primes agrees with the inherited complete-period divisibility law. No independence is asserted without the complete-period or explicit approximation condition.
acceptance: q=(4,9),N=36 gives 1/36 at every tuple, so primality is unnecessary.
q=(2,3),N=5 is a counterexample; at N=6 every tuple has mass 1/6.

nodes.title: Exact joint residue error
nodes.statement: The sum over all tuples a of |J(a)-product_i(1/q(i))| equals 2*R*(Q-R)/(N*Q).
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. All probabilities and normalized expressions below are real.

I is any finite index type, possibly empty; q:I->N has positive values and is pairwise coprime. Put Q=product_i q(i), R=N mod Q, E=ZMod.prodEquivPi q, and J(a)=mu_N({n : for every i, the cast of n in ZMod(q(i)) equals a(i)}). The tuple a lies in the native dependent product of ZMod(q(i)). Moduli 1 and composite coprime moduli are allowed.
proofSteps: Rewrite the model atom as 1/Q and the arithmetic atom using the event identity in crt-residue-probability.
Reindex the finite sum through the native CRT equivalence E. Apply residue-summed-error at the positive product Q.

For N<Q the exact value is 2*(1-N/Q), giving the source small-support obstruction. For all Q the half-error is at most Q/(4N), from R*(Q-R)<=Q^2/4; this is useful when Q/N is small, not a general growing-prime approximation.

nodes.title: Bounded joint residue statistic bound
nodes.statement: For a real function F on residue tuples with L<=F(a)<=U and L<=U, |integral F((cast(n) in ZMod(q(i)))_i) dmu_N - [product_i(1/q(i))]*sum_a F(a)| <= (U-L)*R*(Q-R)/(N*Q).

Moduli 1 and composite coprime moduli are allowed.
F is real-valued on the finite tuple space; L,U are real and L<=U, with pointwise L<=F<=U.
proofSteps: Compose F with the existing CRT equivalence E. Its range remains in [L,U]. The empirical statistic becomes the single-modulus statistic because E preserves natural casts.
Apply residue-statistic-error at Q. Reindex the uniform sum through E, and identify 1/Q with the product of coordinate reciprocal moduli.

Indicators of tuple events have L=0,U=1 and give the event comparison with half the exact summed error. Coordinate products can use any proved finite range bound; no heuristic replacement of arithmetic statistics is assumed.
acceptance: At q=(2,3),N=5, the indicator of all tuples except (0,0) has discrepancy 1/6.
Constants have zero error, and all statistics have zero discrepancy when Q divides N.

nodes.title: Repeated-factor decomposition
nodes.statement: D(n)=sum over p in n.primeFactors of ((n.factorization(p):R)-1). This holds for every natural n, including zero and one under the native zero-extension conventions.
hypotheses: omega and Omega are the existing cardDistinctFactors and cardFactors. Write D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with casts before real subtraction. D is a local expression, not a new arithmetic-function or random-variable definition.
proofSteps: Rewrite the existing Omega as the Finsupp sum of factorization exponents and use support_factorization to index by n.primeFactors.
Rewrite omega as the cardinality of this finite set using cardDistinctFactors_apply, primeFactors and List.card_toFinset. Distribute the real subtraction through the finite sum.
For n=0 or 1 both finite supports are empty. Nonnegativity D(n)>=0 follows directly from List.toFinset_card_le; no real cast of truncated subtraction is silently substituted.
acceptance: D(0)=D(1)=0; D(72)=3 from exponents 3 at 2 and 2 at 3.
A prime power p^k with k>=1 contributes k-1, not k and not merely the indicator of a repeated prime.

nodes.title: Repeated powers of one prime
nodes.statement: Sum over j in the natural closed interval [2,N] of 1_{p^j divides n} equals n.factorization(p)-1, where the right subtraction is natural truncated subtraction.
hypotheses: n,N,p are natural, 0<n<=N, and p is prime.
proofSteps: Use Prime.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization to replace each divisibility test by j<=v, with v=n.factorization(p).
Nat.factorization_lt and n<=N imply v<=N. The filtered interval is exactly [2,v]; Nat.card_Icc gives v+1-2=v-1.
When v=0 or 1 this interval is empty. The assumption n>0 is essential: every prime power divides zero while its native factorization is zero.
acceptance: At n=N=12,p=2 the sum is 1; at p=3 or 5 it is 0.
At n=N=8,p=2 it is 2. Composite p=4,n=N=16 would give 1 on the left but 0 on the right, so primality cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Finite repeated-prime-power expansion
nodes.statement: For 0<n<=N, D(n)=sum over p in Nat.primesLE(N), sum over j in [2,N], 1_{p^j divides n}, with real indicators.
hypotheses: omega and Omega are the existing cardDistinctFactors and cardFactors. Write D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with casts before real subtraction. D is a local expression, not a new arithmetic-function or random-variable definition.
n,N are natural and 0<n<=N; primesLE uses the inclusive native prime cutoff.
proofSteps: Start with excess-factorization. Every supported exponent is positive by Prime.factorization_pos_of_dvd. Thus its real contribution v-1 is the real cast of the natural v-1 from prime-power-tail-count.
Every prime factor p of n satisfies p<=n<=N. Enlarge the prime-factor sum to primesLE(N); outside the support the exponent is zero and the tail count is zero.
Use prime-power-tail-count on each prime. Both cutoffs are finite. N is deliberately a crude exponent bound, avoiding logarithmic rounding conventions.
acceptance: At n=72,N=100 the nonzero terms are (2,2),(2,3),(3,2).
For n=1 or for N=1 the sum is zero. n=0 is excluded, although D(0)=0.

nodes.title: Exact repeated-factor mean
nodes.statement: Integral D dmu_N equals sum over p in primesLE(N), sum over j in [2,N], floor(N/p^j)/N. Natural division is performed before casting to the reals.
hypotheses: omega and Omega are the existing cardDistinctFactors and cardFactors. Write D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with casts before real subtraction. D is a local expression, not a new arithmetic-function or random-variable definition.
m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m on discrete naturals. Only 1,...,N are sampled.
proofSteps: Use integral_empiricalMeasure to express the integral as a finite average. Each sampled n=k+1 satisfies 0<n<=N, so apply excess-prime-power-expansion with this fixed N.
Exchange the three finite sums. The average of each prime-power divisibility indicator is divisibility-probability with positive modulus p^j.
This argument uses counting, not independence; repeated powers of one prime are nested events.
acceptance: At N=4 the mean is 1/4, at N=12 it is 5/12, and at N=16 it is 1/2.
At N=1,2,3 it is zero. No empty-sample normalization is introduced.

nodes.title: Uniform repeated-factor mean bound
nodes.statement: 0<=integral D dmu_N<=1-1/N. In particular the mean is at most 1, uniformly in the positive sample size.
hypotheses: omega and Omega are the existing cardDistinctFactors and cardFactors. Write D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with casts before real subtraction. D is a local expression, not a new arithmetic-function or random-variable definition.
m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m on discrete naturals. Only 1,...,N are sampled.
proofSteps: Nonnegativity follows from omega<=Omega, supplied by the existing list finite-set cardinality bound, and finite empirical integration.
Apply excess-mean-formula and divisibility-error termwise to bound floor(N/p^j)/N by 1/p^j.
For each p>=2 the existing geom_sum_Ico_le_of_lt_one at x=1/p,m=2,n=N+1 bounds the inner sum by (1/p)^2/(1-1/p)=1/[p(p-1)].

Enlarge the nonnegative sum from primes to all integers 2<=r<=N by the existing sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg. Rewrite 1/[r(r-1)]=1/(r-1)-1/r and use the existing sum_Icc_sub telescope to obtain 1-1/N. Treat N=1 separately as an empty sum. No infinite series or Mertens estimate is used.
acceptance: N=1 gives equality zero; N=12 gives 5/12<=11/12.
This is an average bound, not D(n)<=1 pointwise: D(16)=3. It gives no bound on higher moments by itself.

nodes.title: Repeated-factor tail bound
nodes.statement: For every real t>0, mu_N({n : t<=D(n)}).toReal <= (1-1/N)/t.
hypotheses: omega and Omega are the existing cardDistinctFactors and cardFactors. Write D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with casts before real subtraction. D is a local expression, not a new arithmetic-function or random-variable definition.
m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m on discrete naturals. Only 1,...,N are sampled.
t is real and strictly positive.
proofSteps: Apply the existing real Markov inequality to the nonnegative D, whose integrability follows from the finite empirical Dirac decomposition on discrete naturals.
Equivalently, use the empirical indicator formula and the pointwise inequality t*1_{t<=D(n)}<=D(n); summing finite terms proves the same application without any new general Markov lemma.

t=0 is forbidden: the event is the whole sample whereas Lean's totalized division would make the proposed upper bound zero.

nodes.statement: Put X(n)=(omega(n)-b)/s and Y(n)=(Omega(n)-b)/s, with real casts. For every real x, mu_N({X<=x-delta}).toReal-(1-1/N)/(s*delta) <= mu_N({Y<=x}).toReal <= mu_N({X<=x}).toReal.
hypotheses: omega and Omega are the existing cardDistinctFactors and cardFactors. Write D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with casts before real subtraction. D is a local expression, not a new arithmetic-function or random-variable definition.
m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m on discrete naturals. Only 1,...,N are sampled.

proofSteps: The pointwise identity Y=X+D/s and D>=0 give {Y<=x} subset {X<=x}. Apply finite real-measure monotonicity for the upper bound.
If X<=x-delta and Y>x, then D>s*delta. Thus {X<=x-delta} is contained in {Y<=x} union {s*delta<=D}. Apply real-measure subadditivity.
Use excess-tail-bound at t=s*delta and rearrange. The two sides form one sandwich from the same event comparison. There is no continuity assumption because this is a finite inequality.

Convergence of the X laws and a scale tending to infinity make this sandwich an input to transfer at continuity points. Such convergence and the generic CDF/weak-convergence dictionary are still separate obligations, not hypotheses silently discharged here.

nodes.title: Transfer between omega and Omega limit laws
nodes.statement: For arbitrary real centers b_m, a real scale s_m tending to positive infinity, and any Borel probability measure nu on R, (omega-b_m)/s_m under mu_(m+1) converges in distribution to nu if and only if (Omega-b_m)/s_m does. The limit law need not have a continuous CDF.
hypotheses: m is natural, N=m+1, and mu_N is the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m on discrete naturals. Samples are 1,...,N, never zero. Repeated observation values retain their multiplicities.
All law, CDF, characteristic-function and convergence objects are native. nu denotes a Borel probability measure on the real line when present; convergence is along natural m tending to infinity.

Use the existing omega=cardDistinctFactors and Omega=cardFactors, with real casts before subtraction. D=Omega-omega>=0. Put X_m(n)=(omega(n)-b_m)/s_m and Y_m(n)=(Omega(n)-b_m)/s_m with the SAME center and scale. These are local expressions, not new carriers.
proofSteps: All observations are measurable on discrete naturals; their pushforward laws are native probability measures. Use the existing bounded-Lipschitz integral characterization of weak convergence.

For each bounded L-Lipschitz test function g, integral_map rewrites integrals against the two laws as the arithmetic expectations. On the eventual positive-scale tail, excess-lipschitz-bound gives their absolute difference at most L/s_m.

The last bound tends to zero by reciprocal convergence. Apply the eventual squeeze theorem to the absolute difference, then the native metric criterion and addition/subtraction of limits to transfer the limiting integral from either law to the other.
Apply the reverse direction of the same bounded-Lipschitz characterization. No new Slutsky theorem is planned, and its existing fixed-sampling-measure helper is not misapplied.

Specializing the center and scale to the log-log Erdős–Kac normalization is valid once their scale divergence and the omega Gaussian-limit premise are supplied. This checkpoint does not supply the latter; it closes only the repeated-factor transfer in Exercise 51(iv).
acceptance: The equivalence holds for s_m=m+1 and arbitrary common b_m and target probability nu.

nodes.title: Positive geometric expansion at one prime
nodes.statement: For n>0, n<=N and prime p, a^(v_p(n)-1)=1+sum_{j=2}^N 1_{p^j|n}·(1/2)·a^(j-2), where v_p(n)=n.factorization p and both subtractions in natural exponents are truncated.
hypotheses: m,n,N,k are natural. Where m occurs set M=m+1 and use mu_M, the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. Its support is 1,...,M, never zero.

D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with real casts before subtraction and the native cardFactors/cardDistinctFactors. D is nonnegative. Put a=3/2 and t=log(a)>0 only as local scalar notation; no new definition or carrier is exported. All finite sums use their displayed inclusive cutoffs.
proofSteps: Set v=v_p(n). The native divisibility criterion says p^j|n iff j<=v; positivity of n is essential. Native factorization_lt gives v<n<=N.
If v=0 or v=1, the indicated exponent interval contributes nothing and the natural exponent v-1 is zero, so both sides equal one.
For v>=2, reindex j=i+2 over i=0,...,v-2. The native finite geometric identity at a=3/2 gives (1/2)·sum_{i=0}^{v-2}a^i=a^(v-1)-1.
No contribution from j=1 is permitted: the weight measures repeated factors, not all factors.
acceptance: At n=1 and p=2 the local weight is 1.
At n=8 and p=2 the local weight is 9/4.
At n=p=2 the local weight is 1, not 3/2.

nodes.title: Finite Euler upper bound for the excess mean
nodes.statement: For M=m+1, E_mu_M[exp(tD)]<=product_{p<=M, prime}(1+sum_{j=2}^M (1/2)·a^(j-2)/p^j).
hypotheses: m,n,N,k are natural. Where m occurs set M=m+1 and use mu_M, the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. Its support is 1,...,M, never zero.

D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with real casts before subtraction and the native cardFactors/cardDistinctFactors. D is nonnegative. Put a=3/2 and t=log(a)>0 only as local scalar notation; no new definition or carrier is exported. All finite sums use their displayed inclusive cutoffs.
proofSteps: On the positive sample, replace exp(tD) by the finite prime product and then replace each local factor by its positive geometric expansion.

Expand the product using the native finite product-of-sums theorem. At each prime the choices are the constant term or an exponent j in [2,M]. Give the constant choice exponent zero, weight one and modulus p^0=1.

For a chosen exponent family, powers of distinct primes are pairwise coprime by the native theorem. Identify all zero-residue events with divisibility via natCast_eq_zero_iff. The inherited CRT atom formula gives joint probability floor(M/Q)/M for Q=product p^j.

To see the remainder indicator vanish at the zero tuple, its inverse CRT residue is zero and (-1).val=Q-1; the remainder R is always less than Q. This includes Q=1, where R=0. Thus no event is assumed independent.
Every coefficient is nonnegative. Replace floor(M/Q)/M by 1/Q, factor that denominator over the chosen prime powers, and reverse the finite product expansion.
All integration is the native finite empirical sum. There is no limiting product or infinite interchange of sums.

nodes.title: Uniform bound for one repeated-factor Euler term
nodes.statement: For any prime p and natural N, sum_{j=2}^N (1/2)·a^(j-2)/p^j <= 2/p^2.
hypotheses: m,n,N,k are natural. Where m occurs set M=m+1 and use mu_M, the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. Its support is 1,...,M, never zero.

D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with real casts before subtraction and the native cardFactors/cardDistinctFactors. D is nonnegative. Put a=3/2 and t=log(a)>0 only as local scalar notation; no new definition or carrier is exported. All finite sums use their displayed inclusive cutoffs.
proofSteps: If N<2 the sum is empty and the right side is positive.
Otherwise reindex j=i+2. The sum is [1/(2p^2)]·sum_{i=0}^{N-2}(3/(2p))^i.
Since p>=2, the ratio is in (0,3/4], strictly less than one. The native finite geometric bound gives at most 1/[p(2p-3)].
The inequality 1/[p(2p-3)]<=2/p^2 follows by positive cross-multiplication from p>=2. It is equality at p=2 at the infinite-sum bound, not at a finite cutoff.
The fixed base a=3/2 is below 2. At base 2 the local ratio at p=2 is one and this uniform argument fails.
acceptance: For p=2,N=2 the sum is 1/8.
At N=1 the sum is zero for every p.
Replacing a by 2 gives sum_{j=2}^{10}2^(j-2)/2^j=9/4; geometric decay is lost.

nodes.title: Uniform finite excess Euler product bound
nodes.statement: For any finite set P of primes and any natural N, product_{p in P}(1+sum_{j=2}^N (1/2)·a^(j-2)/p^j)<=exp(2).
hypotheses: m,n,N,k are natural. Where m occurs set M=m+1 and use mu_M, the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. Its support is 1,...,M, never zero.

D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with real casts before subtraction and the native cardFactors/cardDistinctFactors. D is nonnegative. Put a=3/2 and t=log(a)>0 only as local scalar notation; no new definition or carrier is exported. All finite sums use their displayed inclusive cutoffs.

Use native prod_one_add_le_exp_sum with the globally nonnegative function n mapped to 2/(n:R)^2; total division at n=0 still gives a nonnegative value. The result is exp(2·sum_{p in P}1/p^2).
Take B=max(2,max P), with any native finite supremum implementing the empty case. Because all p>=2, enlarge the nonnegative sum to integers r=2,...,B.

For r>=2, 1/r^2<=1/[r(r-1)]=1/(r-1)-1/r. The existing additive form generated by prod_Icc_div telescopes the latter finite sum to 1-1/B<=1. The subset-sum monotonicity is the additive form of the recorded native multiplicative supplier.
Monotonicity of exp now gives exp(2). Empty P has product one and satisfies the same bound. No prime-reciprocal asymptotic, Mertens theorem or infinite Euler product enters.

nodes.statement: For every M=m+1>=1, E_mu_M[exp(log(3/2)·D)]<=exp(2), with an absolute constant independent of M.

proofSteps: Apply excess-exponential-euler at M=m+1.
The native primesLE membership theorem supplies primality of every member; apply excess-finite-euler-bound to that finite set with cutoff M.

nodes.title: All fixed repeated-factor moments
nodes.statement: For every natural k and M=m+1, E_mu_M[|D|^k]<=exp(2)·k!/[log(3/2)]^k. In particular sum_{n=1}^M D(n)^k is bounded by M times this explicit k-dependent constant.
hypotheses: m,n,N,k are natural. Where m occurs set M=m+1 and use mu_M, the existing empiricalMeasure of k mapped to k+1 at index m, on discrete naturals. Its support is 1,...,M, never zero.

D(n)=(Omega(n):R)-(omega(n):R), with real casts before subtraction and the native cardFactors/cardDistinctFactors. D is nonnegative. Put a=3/2 and t=log(a)>0 only as local scalar notation; no new definition or carrier is exported. All finite sums use their displayed inclusive cutoffs.
proofSteps: D>=0 follows from distinct-factor cardinality at most total-factor cardinality (or the inherited nonnegative factorization sum). Thus |D|=D, including the arithmetic zero extension.
For t=log(3/2)>0, apply the native inequality (tD)^k/k!<=exp(tD). Both t^k and k! are strictly positive, even for k=0.
Rearrange pointwise to D^k<=[k!/t^k]exp(tD). Average over the finite positive sample using its native sum formula and then apply excess-exponential-mean.

The implied constant depends on k and is not claimed uniform in growing k. At k=0 the actual mean is one. The unnormalized sum version follows by multiplying by M; for a real cutoff x>=1, take M=floor(x)<=x.
This completes the worker proof decomposition of Exercise 46(ii)'s fixed-moment bound, not its surrounding omega variance estimate or the full Hardy-Ramanujan/Erdos-Kac theorems.
acceptance: The zeroth moment is exactly 1 for every positive sample, not zero.
For M=8 the second excess moment is 5/8.
